content.title: When Do The NHL Playoffs Start For The Penguins? Pittsburgh’s First-Round Timeline and Likely Opponent | Sportsnet Pittsburgh
content.text: The Pittsburgh Penguins are back in the playoffs, and there is no mystery left about its seed or its opponent.Pittsburgh clinched its playoff berth with a win over New Jersey on April 9, and the Penguins will finish second in the Metropolitan Division, which means they will open the first round with home-ice advantage. The only thing left to do is prepare for the return of the Battle of Pennsylvania.With the standings finalized, the Penguins are locked into a first-round matchup against the third-place Philadelphia Flyers. It marks the first time these rivals have met in the postseason since 2018, bringing one of the most intense atmospheres in hockey back to the playoff stage.While the Penguins secured their position early, the Flyers battled through the final week of the season to leapfrog the Capitals and Islanders, setting up a high-stakes series that starts this weekend at PPG Paints Arena.When do the NHL playoffs start for the Penguins?The 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs begin on Saturday, April 18. The NHL has already confirmed that date, but Pittsburgh’s exact Game 1 time is still TBD. The league will announce the full Round 1 schedule once the standings are final and opponents are set.BUY NOW: Cheer on the Pens as they go on a run to the Stanley Cup with affordable ticketsPittsburgh’s series should open on April 18 or April 19, depending on the final TV schedule. Since the Pens are locked into second place in the Metro, Games 1 and 2 will both be at home.Who will the Penguins play in the first round?The Penguins first round opponent is officially locked in: the Philadelphia Flyers.The Battle of Pennsylvania returns to the postseason as the Penguins and Flyers prepare for a high-stakes first-round clash. This rivalry is rooted in decades of divisional tension and geographic proximity, often producing some of the most physical and unpredictable hockey in the league. With both teams snapping multi-year playoff droughts — Pittsburgh back for the first time since 2022 and Philadelphia ending a five-season absence — the energy in both PPG Paints Arena and Xfinity Mobile Arena will be at a fever pitch.Fans still vividly remember the 2018 first-round matchup, which served as a masterclass in offensive dominance for Pittsburgh. In that six-game series, the Penguins’ stars overwhelmed the Flyers, highlighted by an opening 7-0 blowout and a decisive 8-5 victory in Game 6 to clinch the series. While many of the faces have changed since that high-scoring affair, the veteran leadership of Sidney Crosby and Evgeni Malkin remains the backbone of a Penguins squad looking to replicate that postseason success against their cross-state rivals.Philadelphia enters this series with a rejuvenated roster led by Travis Konecny and the dynamic Trevor Zegras, both of whom have cleared the 65-point mark this season. The Flyers also boast one of the league's most exciting young talents in Matvei Michkov, whose creative playmaking adds a new layer to their attack. Defensively, the Flyers rely on the steady presence of Travis Sanheim and the elite goaltending of Dan Vladar, who has been the team's MVP throughout a resurgent 2025-26 campaign.What dates should Penguins fans circle?Pittsburgh still has regular-season business left before the bracket is final. The Penguins have one game left: a road game at St. Louis.The key dates:Tuesday, April 14: Penguins at BluesSaturday, April 18: Stanley Cup Playoffs beginSo the Pittsburgh version of the playoff countdown is pretty clean. The Pens already know they are hosting Round 1 against their cross-state rival Flyers. Now, it's just counting down the days until Game 1 at PPG Paints Arena.
